absent: Locking, TLB invalidation and memory ordering for early table population and entry area setup.
Exact virtual to shadow translation formula and shadow memory scale.
Allocator fallback and failure handling beyond the fatal flag in early boot.
Per CPU offset layout and per CPU entry area contents.
Traversal order, locking and callback contract of the generic page table dump iterator.
Protection bit encodings and conversion between small and large protections.

findings.text: Init entry maps a virtual range into KASAN shadow by aligning the translated start down and the translated end up to page granularity and then populating that shadow interval for the given node.

Shadow population normalizes the interval to page boundaries and walks the top level in bounded subranges to the end, creating missing intermediate tables on demand in the initial address space and descending at each level, while leaving already present leaf mappings untouched at lower levels.
At the leaf table level the walker visits each page slot in the interval, skips occupied entries, otherwise obtains a fresh page for the requesting node and installs it with kernel page protection.

When the processor advertises large page support and a subrange exactly covers one aligned large block, the middle levels first attempt a single large mapping with a non failing large allocation and release that block on install failure before falling back to allocating a regular table page.

Early page allocation requests node aware memblock memory bounded below the accessible limit and either returns possibly null memory or terminates boot with a diagnostic identifying caller and node when failure is marked fatal.

Large mapping installers first require uniform memory type over the whole large span, then refuse already populated table entries that are not leaves, otherwise install a converted large entry and report success as a boolean while failure leaves the entry unchanged.
Early CPU to node lookup prefers the early per CPU map when available, otherwise warns with a stack trace and reports no node for an impossible processor, else returns the regular per CPU mapping.

32 bit extra mapping helpers derive table indices from the virtual address, allocate a low page and link it with table presence when the parent entry is empty, verify the fresh table matches the kernel offset view, and return the addressed child entry.

64 bit extra mapping helpers resolve the kernel top entry for the address and descend through per level fill helpers that allocate a missing next level page in the initial address space, logging a mismatch diagnostic if the allocated page disagrees with the offset view, finally returning the addressed leaf entry.

Entry area initialization prepares per CPU offsets, establishes the reserved mapping on 32 bit after checking total size and base alignment and stepping by large block size with wraparound protection, instantiates each possible processor area, then synchronizes the initial table as the final essential update.
Initial table synchronization copies the kernel portion of the main directory into the boot directory and additionally mirrors a bounded prefix of the low identity portion for stub use.

Dump state combines generic walker state with current level, current and effective protections, per level accumulated protections, run start, marker cursor, line counts, output destination selectors, writable executable accounting, and sequence handle; marker entries pair a start address with a display name and optional line cap.

Marker tables enumerate user then kernel regions in address order with human names, use zero placeholders for runtime filled bases, include conditional entries for optional features, terminate with a maximal address sentinel, and select distinct initial roots per word size.
Each level span is the child entry count multiplied by the next lower level span, rooted at one page, giving nested coverage sizes from page through top level.

Core walker selects full or split address ranges by word size, wires per level note and effective protection callbacks, starts before any level with output and checking options, performs the walk, then when checking reports either failure with a count or success and returns the verdict; debug wrappers choose user or kernel root under isolation and dmesg wrapper forces kernel walk to the log.

Diagnostic viewers expose kernel, current kernel, optionally current user under isolation, and optionally EFI tables as read only debug entries that do nothing when the target root is absent, created under a page tables directory at init and removed recursively at exit.

Effective protection masks each entry to flag bits, takes the top level directly, and for deeper levels intersects user and writable permissions with the parent while unioning the no execute attribute, with dedicated adapters per table depth.

Page noter coalesces consecutive entries with identical raw and effective protections at the same level within one marker region, emitting the finished run as an address interval plus scaled size and flag rendering on each break, advancing markers with elision summaries when capped, performing an optional writable executable check before emission, and flushing through a distinct empty entry.

Flag rendering prints blanks for non present entries, otherwise a fixed column set for privilege, writability, cache controls, level dependent large versus attribute indication, global and execute state, followed by the level name.

Writable executable accounting converts run length to pages, exempts the platform firmware window with a one time notice, otherwise accumulates the count and warns once with the run start when no execute support exists; large mapping refusal due to mixed memory types is reported once with the affected range for one size.

Dump output helpers send formatted text either to the kernel log or to the supplied sequence object depending on the destination flag, guarding against a null sequence, with a continuing form that appends to the current line.
